html:
The Huni Kuin, also called Kaxinawá or Cashinahua, are a Panoan-speaking people of the western Amazon, living along the Purus, Tarauacá, Jordão and other rivers in Acre state, Brazil, and across the border in Peru. Huni Kuin means "true people".

They grow manioc, maize and bananas, hunt and fish. They are known for kene, fine geometric designs painted on bodies and woven into cloth, and for ceremonies with ayahuasca, which they call nixi pae. The rubber boom of the late 1800s brought rubber bosses who took their land and forced many into labour. Since the 1980s they have won legal title to many territories in Brazil, and their art and songs have become widely known. Their relatives include the Kaxarari and other Panoan peoples.
